note: Statement moves dealt by scripts/deal.mjs. Each move is a way to make the first screen ownable while the five-second line keeps it clear. Observed examples are audited records in research/sites.json (one browser, one date each).

moves.name: A character with a job
moves.what: An original character drawn from the product's subject that does one job in the story: it demonstrates the product, reacts to the visitor's action, or carries the result.
moves.fits: Consumer and prosumer products, products people use daily or emotionally, crowded categories where recall matters, developer tools with a playful culture.
moves.avoid_when: The buyer is a regulated or high-stakes enterprise committee and the character would be the only thing on the first screen; the character would only decorate.
moves.first_screen: The character holds, uses or reacts to the product's real output next to the five-second line; it never stands alone as the hero.
moves.build: Rigged SVG of 6-10 parts with a locked face and one accent part (see references/statement.md, characters).
observed: vanta: a line-drawn llama recurring across hero and audience cards
phantom: the ghost mark set inline inside headlines as a glyph
finni-health: a cartoon fox recurring across sections with illustrated scenes
doomersion: the mascot recurs inside the app screens

moves.name: An inhabited world
moves.what: The first screen is a place from the visitor's own world (a kitchen pass, a trading floor, a clinic hallway) drawn or built so the product visibly lives in it; nav, headline and action are working parts set inside the world.
moves.fits: Products tied to a physical or social setting; operations software; marketplaces; anything whose user works somewhere specific.
moves.avoid_when: The world would be a generic office or a desk with a laptop; the scene would push the five-second line below the fold on phones.
moves.first_screen: A single scene at a scale where the product's effect is visible inside it (a ticket printing, a shelf restocking), with the five-second line in clear space.
moves.build: One graphic language: flat tone steps or a single texture treatment across scene, charts and icons; three levels of detail; a still that reads without motion.
observed: meuze: a halftone restaurant scene pinned through a long scroll track, one dot-matrix treatment across photo, charts and logo
finni-health: illustrated bedtime and garden scenes in full-width colour bands
posthog: a product suite presented as a place to explore

moves.name: The product as a toy
moves.what: The first screen is the core interaction, playable with real content in seconds, no sign-up: type, drag, scrub, toggle, and the product's output answers.
moves.fits: Tools whose value shows in one action: generators, editors, calculators, converters, APIs with a visible response, schedulers.
moves.avoid_when: The real interaction needs data the visitor does not have, or takes minutes; a fake toy that ignores input is worse than none.
moves.first_screen: The control is focused or obvious, the default state already shows a good result, and one sentence says it runs locally or on sample data.
moves.build: Bounded inputs, visible progress, reset, keyboard path and the artifact stress test; the finished state is the static fallback.
observed: tldraw: a live, drawable canvas beside the install command and a ten-line example
flora: a draggable node graph proves the product after generated output

moves.name: An object portrait
moves.what: The product, or its output, shown as one physical or physical-feeling object at heroic scale: a device, a printed report, a card, a receipt, a package.
moves.fits: Hardware; products whose output is a document or artifact; financial products with a card or statement; anything that can be held.
moves.avoid_when: There is no honest object (an abstract platform) and the object would be a stand-in metaphor.
moves.first_screen: One object, lit and scaled to dominate, with real labels on it and the five-second line beside it.
moves.build: HTML or SVG object built from the product's real fields (not an image of text); a poster frame first; at most one rotation or reveal.
observed: button-computer: a full-bleed video of the device clipped to a person
nori: a physical product image leading to task examples and a direct order action

moves.name: The audience's own notation
moves.what: The page borrows a format the visitor reads every day and the product produces or changes: a ticket, a chart, a score, a ledger line, a recipe card, a lab plate, a shipping label.
moves.fits: Vertical software for a trade with its own documents; B2B tools where the buyer recognises the format instantly.
moves.avoid_when: The format is a costume (monospace labels on a non-technical product) or the visitor would not recognise it.
moves.first_screen: The notation is the hero artifact, filled with the product's result, at a size where it reads; the headline speaks the trade's words.
moves.build: Recreate the format in semantic HTML from real fields; keep its conventions (columns, codes, stamps) and drop chrome that is only decoration.
observed: end-close: a matching table with an 'Agent resolved' toast
canary: replayed failures and diffs as the proof sequence

moves.name: A typographic statement
moves.what: The type is the image: one set phrase or the wordmark at monumental scale, composed so the letters themselves carry the idea.
moves.fits: Products with a strong single word or claim; brands with a distinctive commissioned or open-licence face; developer and design tools.
moves.avoid_when: The phrase needs more than two lines at 390px; the product needs to be seen to be believed.
moves.first_screen: At most two lines at every width; the five-second line and the action immediately beneath; the product artifact begins at the fold.
moves.build: Size from the measured corpus upward deliberately (HR-04); one face, tight leading, no gradient text, no single accented word.
observed: canary: a two-line poster headline on a yellow highlight bar
granola: a large serif promise beside a typing meeting-note mock
gutgutgoose and astro-mechanica: a giant wordmark closing the page

moves.name: A data portrait
moves.what: The product's real or sample data drawn as a striking image: a forecast curve, a network, a heat map, a timeline, labelled so it reads as information first.
moves.fits: Analytics, forecasting, infrastructure and finance products whose output is a pattern people care about.
moves.avoid_when: The chart would be a fake dashboard of grey bars; the data has no story at a glance.
moves.first_screen: One chart with one annotated moment (the spike, the anomaly, the saved hour), sized as a picture, not a dashboard tile.
moves.build: SVG from a small dataset in the page; real axes and units; the annotation is text, not only colour.
observed: meuze: a forecast curve with a match-day spike as an operational artifact

moves.name: Before and after
moves.what: The first screen holds the visitor's current mess and the product's result side by side, or one object that changes from one to the other under the visitor's control.
moves.fits: Products that clean, convert, translate, summarise, reconcile, schedule or fix.
moves.avoid_when: The before state would mock the customer, or the after state would need invented metrics.
moves.first_screen: Both states visible or one control away; a real example labelled as a sample.
moves.build: One slider, toggle or step control; both states readable as stills; no auto-flip faster than reading speed.
observed: finni-health: eligibility input ahead of the headline answers the first question directly

moves.name: A generative system
moves.what: A rule-based visual made from the product's own logic (a scheduler's grid, a compiler's tree, a router's paths), animated or seeded, so the image is the product's idea.
moves.fits: Infrastructure, AI research, developer platforms, products whose mechanism is beautiful but invisible.
moves.avoid_when: The rule has nothing to do with the product (particles for their own sake); text contrast would depend on the animation.
moves.first_screen: The system as background or side panel with the five-second line on a stable ground; it settles within five seconds and has a still frame.
moves.build: Canvas or SVG, seeded so every capture matches; pauses off-screen and under reduced motion; idles within 5 s (MO-05).
observed: reflection-ai: a slowly drifting dot-matrix canvas as the hero's only image
modal: a self-assembling dot-matrix cube behind a one-line claim

moves.name: A voice with a point of view
moves.what: The first screen is a sharp, specific opinion in the founders' voice, set with editorial care; the product proof arrives immediately below.
moves.fits: Category creators, contrarian products, research labs, small teams selling through belief.
moves.avoid_when: The opinion is generic; the buyer needs to see the product before trusting a stance.
moves.first_screen: The opinion as the headline, the five-second line under it in plain words, one action, and the product artifact cut by the fold.
moves.build: Editorial type pairing, generous measure control, real author attribution; no manifesto wall of text.
observed: traverse: an unstyled text memo
agency and mindy: a signed letter as the whole homepage when the company winds down

canon.name: Canon (the plain page done perfectly)
canon.what: No statement move: the conventional structure for the category, executed with exact type, real product proof and no template tells.
canon.use_when: Only when the person asked for convention, or the buyer's risk is such that any move would cost trust; record why. Never the default.

worlds: objects the user handles at work
documents and forms the user reads
rituals and routines of the user's day
the place where the work happens
the marks, codes and notations of the trade
tools and materials of the craft
the sound, rhythm or timing of the work
the graphic tradition of the user's culture or region
